content: 1. Lanzieri T, Redd S, Abernathy E, and Icenogle J authored Chapter 15, titled Congenital Rubella Syndrome, which is included in the Manual for the Surveillance of Vaccine-Preventable Diseases, edited by Roush SW, Baldy LM, and Hall MAK. This document was accessed on July 21, 2022. 2. Zimmerman LA, Knapp JK, Antoni S, Grant GB, and Reef SE documented global progress toward the control and elimination of rubella and congenital rubella syndrome (CRS) from 2012 to 2020. Their findings were published in the MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2022, Volume 71, Issue 6, pages 196–201. 3. Khanal S, Bahl S, Sharifuzzaman M, Dhongde D, Pattamadilok S, Reef S, and colleagues reported on advancements in controlling rubella and CRS in the South-East Asia Region between 2000 and 2016. Their work appeared in the MMWR Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report in 2018, Volume 67, Issue 21, pages 602–606. 4. Shanmugasundaram D, Awasthi S, Dwibedi B, Geetha S, Jain M, Malik S, and others assessed the burden of congenital rubella syndrome in India using data from cross-sectional serosurveys conducted in 2017 and 2019–2020. Their research was published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2021, Volume 15, Issue 7, under the identifier e0009608. 5. The development of the technical document was guided strategically by Dr. Poonam Khetrapal Singh, Regional Director of WHO SEARO, along with Dr. Pem Namgyal, Director of Programme Management, and Dr. Suman Rijal, Director of CDS. Oversight of the process was provided by Dr. Sunil Bahl, Coordinator of COVAX, Immunization, and Vaccine Development. 6. Dr. Sudhir Khanal (IVD/CDS, WHO SEARO) led the coordination and development of the technical document in collaboration with Dr. Sudhir Joshi (IVD/CDS, WHO SEARO). WHO Consultant Dr. Lalit Kant played a critical role in updating the technical content of the document. 7. The document benefited from expert input provided by participants of the Regional Workshop held in Dhaka from June 13–16, 2022. This workshop reviewed progress toward measles-rubella and other priority vaccine-preventable disease (VPD) surveillance, outbreak preparedness, and response in the WHO South-East Asia Region. Participants included National EPI Programme Managers, VPD Surveillance Officers from Member States, WHO country office staff, UNICEF representatives, and other external collaborators. 8. WHO Headquarters staff, including Dr. Anindya Bose and Dr. Heidi Soeters, reviewed the draft surveillance standard document and provided technical inputs. 9. WHO SEARO contributors included Dr. Jayantha Liyanage, Dr. Sigrun Roesel, Dr. Emmanuel Njambe, Dr. Lucky Sangal, Dr. Pankaj Bhatnagar, Ms. Uttara Aggarwal, Mr. Sharifuzzaman, Dr. Rajendra Bohara, Dr. Ariful Islam, Dr. Tanbir Islam, Dr. Subramanya Balakuntlam Pattabhiramaiah, Dr. Ratnesh Murugan, Dr. Stephen Chacko, Dr. Paba Palihawadana, Dr. Aishath Thimna Latheef, Dr. Balwinder Chawla, Dr. Khaing Khaing Gyi, Dr. Vinod Bura, Dr. Rahul Pradhan, Dr. Pasang Rai, Dr. Preshila Samarawera, Ms. Aree Moungsookjareoun, and Dr. Sudath Peiris. 10. UNICEF’s Christopher Gregory provided inputs and coordinated contributions from the UNICEF team for various sections of the document. 11. From the US CDC, Dr. Ahmed Kassem and Dr. Michelle Morales contributed to multiple sections of the document and coordinated inputs from various teams within the CDC.
